question: Will the European Council's 26–27 November 2026 conclusions explicitly reference the EU's 22nd sanctions package against Russia?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: recent European Council conclusions name pending or just-adopted Russia sanctions packages by ordinal at most meetings (June 2026 called for the 21st, October 2026 welcomed it; similar in 2025), including texts 'firmly supported by 26'. Key update: the 12 Nov Costa/von der Leyen joint statement explicitly ties the Commission's 22nd package presentation to this summit, Kallas (16 Nov) says presentation is 'in the coming days', and adoption is targeted for Christmas, so a 'calls for swift adoption of the 22nd package' line is the natural template. Main counterarguments: this is a special MFF/Ukraine-financing summit that could deadlock (Merz linkage) and produce no Ukraine text or only narrow MFF conclusions; the package could slip past presentation; the wording could be generic. No human prediction market found.
calls.dossier:
- 12 Nov 2026 (Steptoe sanctions update 16 Nov; Detroit News/Reuters 12 Nov): Costa and von der Leyen joint statement in Dublin says the Commission will present its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia in parallel with the Ukraine 2027 financing proposal, ahead of or at the 26-27 Nov European Council. Commission still debating details (banks, crypto platforms, third-country circumvention; possibly athletes ban, visa limits on ex-combatants).
- 16 Nov 2026 (UNN): Kallas after the Foreign Affairs Council: 'In the coming days, we will present the 22nd package of sanctions.' Journalist Rikard Jozwiak: confidential talks start this week, approval targeted by Christmas, 23rd package around Feb 2027.
- 16 Nov 2026 (Council press release): 113 new listings (101 entities, 12 individuals); the Commission said this is not the 22nd package.
- Precedent (question background): June 2026 conclusions 'call for the swift adoption of the 21st sanctions package'; Oct 2026 conclusions 'welcome the recent adoption of the 21st sanctions package'. From memory, not verified this run: the 2025 conclusions (March and June) also named packages by ordinal, sometimes in Ukraine texts 'firmly supported by 26'.
- Meeting type: a special European Council on the 2028-2034 budget (MFF) and Ukraine's roughly €70bn 2027 funding gap; Merz is linking the two; risk of deadlock or narrow conclusions. An earlier 2026 summit (eualive) ended inconclusively without a budget deal.
- Base rate (class: EUCO meetings 2025-26 held while a numbered package was pending or just adopted): an ordinal reference appeared in most such meetings. The component rate for special or single-topic summits without a full Ukraine section is lower and was not counted.
- Resolution instrument: resolves on the conclusions, statements of heads of state or government and annexes on the Council meeting page (Ukraine texts backed by 26 count); not on drafts, individual leaders' remarks or the Commission's proposal. The ordinal '22nd'/'twenty-second' is required.
- Event window: texts issued for the 26-27 Nov 2026 meeting; as of 17 Nov the meeting has not started (0% elapsed).
- Searched, not found: draft conclusions for 26-27 Nov (Council doc ST-15670-2026 of 13 Nov could not be parsed); any Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker market on this; the exact date the Commission presents the package.

calls.reasoning: Base: the European Council named the pending or adopted package by number in its June and October 2026 conclusions, and the Costa/von der Leyen 12 Nov joint statement links the 22nd package to this summit; Kallas said on 16 Nov it would be presented 'in coming days', so a 'calls for swift adoption of the 22nd package' line is natural. Against: this is a special summit on the MFF and Ukraine's 2027 financing, which is contentious (Merz ultimatum; HU/SK/CZ/BG refusing to fund) and could produce MFF-only or no conclusions, and a financing-focused Ukraine text might mention sanctions only generically. Rough split: about 25% no Ukraine/sanctions text at all; given a text, about 65% it names the 22nd package. No human prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- 12 Nov 2026 (Costa/von der Leyen joint statement, Dublin; reported by Xinhua and Steptoe 16 Nov): 'At the European Council on 26-27 November, Ukraine's urgent financing needs for 2027 will be discussed, based on the Commission's proposal. The Commission will in parallel present its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia.' Steptoe paraphrases this as presenting the package 'at the European Council meeting'. A Reuters/Detroit News headline says 'by year-end'.
- 16 Nov 2026 (Interfax-Ukraine): after the Foreign Affairs Council, Kallas said 'in the coming days we will present the 22nd package of sanctions'. No adoption date was given.
- 16 Nov 2026 (Council): 113 individuals and entities were listed (shadow fleet, revenue sectors); the Commission says this is not the 22nd package.
- Expected package content (Reuters via Steptoe): banks, crypto platforms, third-country circumvention; other reports add refineries, shadow fleet, a possible ban on Russian/Belarusian athletes. The Commission is still debating details.
- Agenda (Costa 13 Nov informal summit; NV/censor reports): two items only, the MFF 2028-2034 and Ukraine's 2027 financing needs. Special meeting.
- Contention: Merz threatens to block the MFF unless all member states commit to Ukraine financing; Hungary, Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Bulgaria reportedly rule out funding (eualive). An updated MFF negotiating box is due before the summit.
- October 2026 draft conclusions (Yahoo exclusive) called for 'further (sanctions) measures'; the final October text 'welcomed the adoption of the 21st sanctions package' (per question background). June 2026 conclusions 'called for swift adoption of the 21st package'.
- Noise: some outlets (Tasnim, Nexus Europa, Penningtons, Izvestia) claim a '22nd package' was adopted on 12 Oct 2026, which conflicts with the October conclusions welcoming the 21st. This looks like a numbering mix-up; a different ordinal resolves NO.
- Status quo: no 22nd package proposed as of 17 Nov; conclusions not yet published.
- Base-rate notes: in regular 2022-2026 European Councils with a Ukraine section, sanctions packages were often named by number when one was pending or just adopted (June/Oct 2026 examples). Special single-topic summits (e.g., Feb 2020 MFF: no conclusions; Feb 2024 Ukraine Facility special) are less consistent; I could not verify whether the Feb 2024 or Dec 2025 texts named a package number.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the final texts on the Council meeting page, including texts 'firmly supported by N' leaders and MFF conclusions; not drafts, the Commission proposal, or individual leaders' statements.
- Event window: the 26-27 Nov 2026 meeting's published texts; as of 17 Nov, 0% elapsed (the meeting has not started).

calls.reasoning: Base rate: EUCO Ukraine texts in 2026 named the pending package by ordinal once it had been proposed or announced by name (March 2026: 20th; June 2026: 21st), but used generic language before that (Dec 2025: 'the next sanctions package'). Here the Commission has publicly committed to present the 22nd package at or just before the 26-27 Nov summit, and the Costa/von der Leyen joint statement already names it, which favours naming. Risks: the special summit centres on the MFF and Ukraine's 2027 financing amid Merz's ultimatum, so it may publish no Ukraine text or one limited to financing; and whether the package is tabled in time is unconfirmed. Estimate ~0.8 (a qualifying text exists, incl. 'firmly supported by 26') x ~0.65 (it names the 22nd). Markets: no matching market found; Polymarket only has adoption-by-date contracts, a different contract.
calls.dossier:
- 12 Nov 2026 (Dublin): von der Leyen said the Commission will present its 22nd sanctions package and its 2027 Ukraine financing proposal before or at the next EUCO. The Costa/vdL joint statement says 'The Commission will in parallel present its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia.' Steptoe (16 Nov) reports the package is to be presented at the 26-27 Nov EUCO. Content still being finalised: banks, crypto, circumvention via third countries.
- 16 Nov 2026: the Council listed 113 individuals and entities (shadow fleet, revenue sectors) plus hybrid/FIMI listings. The Commission says this is not the 22nd package.
- Agenda (Costa, 11 Nov): only two items, MFF 2028-34 and Ukraine's 2027 financing (gap ~EUR70bn). Merz ties his MFF support to all member states funding Ukraine. HU/SK/CZ/BG reluctant to contribute. Agence Europe says the linkage divides the EU27.
- EUCO precedents: Dec 2025 Ukraine text said 'continue to work on the next sanctions package' (unnamed; the 20th had not been proposed yet). 19 Mar 2026 text: 'looks forward to swift adoption of the 20th sanctions package' (named, already proposed). 18-19 Jun 2026: 'calls for the swift adoption of the 21st sanctions package'. 15-16 Oct 2026: 'welcome the recent adoption of the 21st sanctions package'. Jun 2025 text (26 supporters) reportedly called for 'a new package' (unnamed in snippet).

- Special or contentious budget summits have in the past ended without conclusions (e.g. Feb 2020 MFF).
- Resolves off the published EUCO conclusions or statements of heads of state or government for 26-27 Nov 2026, not the Commission proposal or leaders' remarks. Requires the ordinal '22nd/twenty-second' applied to a Russia sanctions package.
- Event window: texts issued for the 26-27 Nov 2026 meeting (final version governs); as of 17 Nov the meeting has not started (0% elapsed).

calls.reasoning: European Council conclusions in 2026 named pending or adopted packages by number (20th in March, 21st in June and October) once the package was announced. The 12 Nov Costa/von der Leyen statement ties the 22nd package to this summit, and the Commission will table it before 26 Nov. The main risk is the special two-item summit (2028-2034 budget plus Ukraine 2027 financing) deadlocking over Merz's linkage, giving no Ukraine text or a financing-only text. A text backed by 26 leaders counts. Estimate: about 0.78 that a qualifying text exists x about 0.78 that it names the 22nd = about 0.6. No market found.
calls.reconciliation: Factual checks: (1) Has the 22nd package been tabled? Searches show it has not as of 17 Nov; Femida and Georgia Today say it will be presented before the 26 Nov summit, and one report says leaders 'will assess' it there, so timing risk is low. (2) Draft conclusions: none found, so this is still unresolved. (3) Agenda: confirmed as a special summit on the 2028-2034 budget plus Ukraine financing (eunews). The remaining disputes are judgment: whether a Ukraine text appears and whether it names the package. I put about 0.78 on each, because the Ukraine financing item makes some Ukraine text likely, a text backed by 26 counts, and the summit is explicitly linked to the 22nd package, against the record of special summits producing narrow texts. My number sits above Runs 2 and 3, which underweight the explicit linkage, and below Run 1, which underweights the risk of a single-topic summit. No market found.
